newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS TO WATCH TODAY - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS TO WATCH TODAY - AUG 7.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australian tobacco group W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd said it had been forced to suspend sales to assess the full implication of a "draconian" increase in tobacco excise announced earlier on Wednesday and is seeking a 48-hour trading halt for its shares from Thursday morning. This follows the announcement by the Federal government of a 200 percent increase in excise on tobacco products, Wills said. It said the excise change will lead to a A$500 million increase in total revenue collected by the Federal government, states and territories.

Soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd showed the impact of its latest acquisition on Wednesday, boosting its net profit by A$40 million from three months of trading in the Philippines. However, sales revenue growth in Europe for the first half ended June 30 was below expectations and the company warned floods there could adversely impact the second half. CCL posted an interim net profit, excluding Philppines earnings, of A$58.1 million, in line with forecasts of around A$60 million and steady on A$57.8 million a year earlier.

Business services company Ausdoc Group Ltd said on Thursday it has agreed to buy the express freight services business of New Zealand's Freightways Ltd for NZ$125 million. Ausdoc said the purchase would be earnings per share positive in the first 12 months of ownership after amortisation of A$3 million in goodwill associated with the acquisition.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.99 (+0.12)
The sudden departure of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) Minerals Division chief, Dick Carter, signalled a major shakeup for the group's coal assets, analysts said on Wednesday.

"In terms of BHP's coal operations something has to give, productivity is just too low," a Melbourne-based analyst said. The analyst speculated the timing of the announcement of Carter's retirement along with a statement saying the results of the last phase of BHP's strategic review would be announced in the next few weeks, heralded big changes for Carter's division.

Clothing retailer Country Road Ltd said on Wednesdaty subdued trading conditions in Australasia in the second half of the year to June 30 meant full year profits may be lower than the profit reported for the first half.
